history.heading: Colonial history
paragraphs: Grenada, a volcanic island in the southern Caribbean along with Carriacou and Petite Martinique, was inhabited by Kalinago people who resisted early colonisation. French settlers conquered the island in the 1650s; according to tradition, the last Kalinago defenders leapt from a cliff at Sauteurs rather than surrender.
Britain took Grenada in 1763. Plantations of sugar, then cocoa and nutmeg, used enslaved Africans. Fédon's Rebellion in 1795–96 briefly challenged British rule. Slavery was abolished in 1834.

history.heading: Independence and revolution
paragraphs: Grenada became independent on 7 February 1974 under Eric Gairy. In 1979 the New Jewel Movement led by Maurice Bishop overthrew Gairy in a bloodless coup and established a revolutionary government with ties to Cuba.

In October 1983 a hard-line faction killed Bishop, and days later the United States invaded with Caribbean allies, restoring elections. Hurricane Ivan devastated the island in 2004, and Hurricane Beryl struck Carriacou in 2024.

culture.heading: The Spice Isle
paragraphs: English is official, and Grenadian Creole is widely spoken. Most people are Christian. Spicemas, the island's carnival in August, features calypso, soca and the jab jab masqueraders covered in black oil.
Oil down, a stew of breadfruit, salted meat and coconut milk, is the national dish. Athlete Kirani James won Olympic gold in the 400 metres in 2012.

politics.heading: Parliamentary democracy
paragraphs: Grenada is a parliamentary democracy and a Commonwealth realm, with the British monarch represented by a governor-general. The prime minister leads the government. The New National Party and the National Democratic Congress are the main parties.

economy.heading: Spices and tourism
paragraphs: Grenada is known as the "Spice Isle" and is one of the world's largest producers of nutmeg and mace, which appear on its flag. Tourism, including cruise ships and yachting, and education, through St. George's University medical school, are major industries.
A citizenship-by-investment programme brings revenue. The currency is the Eastern Caribbean dollar.
